analysis: The installer change adds bind_provider_coordinator and provider_websocket_url (install.sh ~lines 243-300). The provider is bound to the coordinator that served the installer by rewriting only the [coordinator] url line in provider.toml. The host is regex-validated (^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?$), so awk -v injection and TOML injection are mitigated. Plain ws is allowed only for localhost and 127.0.0.1. Production is left unchanged. The signed-app verification and the pinned designated requirement are unchanged, and there is no privileged action. The only security-relevant interaction is the persistent endpoint binding under T-040 (Host-derived installer URL); it is reported as a low finding. The paired tests in coordinator/api/install_sh_test.go only exercise the --bind-coordinator-test path and add os/exec. The new tool coordinator/cmd/devnet-seed/main.go inserts synthetic users, API keys, ledger and balance rows into the database named by EIGENINFERENCE_DATABASE_URL. It guards by refusing to run when users has rows, checked before migration. That guard is the only protection against use on a real database, and the first-run check depends on the search_path (to_regclass('users')). main_test.go uses throwaway databases. seed.go (484326d14bdd807b) was supplied as metadata only, with no content, so it was NOT reviewed. The next pass should check how it generates API keys (predictable or logged plaintext, hashing), whether the seeded ledger and balance data is isolated from production, and whether the binary is built or shipped in a production image. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

findings.detail: bind_provider_coordinator (install.sh, line ~278) writes the COORD_URL baked into the served installer into [coordinator] url in provider.toml for any coordinator other than the production URL. The host regex accepts any https host. When the coordinator has no baseURL set, the installer URL is derived from the request Host header (see the 'derives from request host when baseURL unset' test, T-040). A poisoned or cached installer response, or a spoofed Host, would then give an attacker host a persistent provider registration endpoint. That endpoint would receive the provider's login and API token and its attestation material on every later `darkbloom start`. Before this change, the effect was limited to the install-time download. The bundle hash and Developer ID signature checks still protect the binary. Fix: require baseURL to be configured in production, or restrict the bound host to an allowlist. Also document the persistence in the T-040 mitigations.
findings.title: Installer now persists the serving coordinator URL into provider.toml, widening Host-header-injection impact
